$schema_note: Pinned reference for the v1 meta-tier basal-phenotype report card. v1 pins these values to a BLESSED current-model ensemble run (no biological judgement yet — judgement comes later, from reading drift against the pin). A model 'passes' the card if its basal ensemble reproduces every graded axis within tol_rel. A null reference is ungraded, not a failure.

stimulus.ensemble: 4 seeds x 8 gens, generation_lower_bound=3 -> 20 cells (17 divided); 29/32 generations divided
stimulus.cache_provenance: FULL-mode ParCa cache (out/cache_full), built via v2ecoli-parca --mode full then build_cache.py. The shipped fixture models/parca/parca_state.pkl.gz is FAST-mode (reduced TF set) and does NOT support sustained multi-gen division — reproducing this pin requires a full ParCa run. NB: cache_version inputs_hash (36f7930256f9bc44) is identical for fast and full caches; it hashes code/inputs, not sim_data content, so it will not flag a fast<->full swap.
stimulus.requires_fix: Sustained multi-gen division requires CovertLab/v2ecoli#127 (MarkDPeriod divide-flag detection for generations >= 1).

observed_spread.note: Cell-to-cell CV from the blessed ensemble; tolerances are set comfortably above the mean's standard error (CV/sqrt(n)) so seed-to-seed reproducibility noise does not trip the gate, while still catching real drift.

findings: RNA == rRna for v1 (analysis_runner._MASS_COLS pulls rRna only; ~80-85% of total RNA). Extend to total RNA (tRna+mRna) as a follow-up.

3 of 32 generations did not divide (ran to the 3600 s cap); their over-grown cells are still included in the composition average (n=20). A v1 refinement would restrict composition to divided cells; the effect is small (composition fractions are per-dry-weight and robust).
